what: The heuristic precomputes customer visited/location fact bindings, identifies the depot from the initially true location fact, and reconstructs a dense directed routing-cost matrix from grounded `visit` and `return-to-depot` operator metric costs. It optionally resolves exact `load()`, `capacity()`, and per-customer `demand(...)` PNEs; if capacity or demand PNEs were folded away, it safely disables only the resource-aware component. At evaluation, it identifies the current location and unvisited customers, then builds a nearest-neighbour completion ending at the depot. When complete resource data is available, customers that exceed residual capacity are skipped and a depot transition is inserted when no customer fits.
why: CVRP states are naturally summarized by current location, the unvisited customer set, and residual vehicle capacity. A constructive nearest-neighbour continuation is inexpensive at O(n²), gives a much more informative estimate than customer counts or a pure minimum-edge bound, and strongly rewards geographically coherent routes in the clustered Euclidean-style instances shown. Capacity-aware depot breaks reflect the domain's key route-segmentation decision when exact resource PNEs survive translation, while operator-derived costs avoid unsafe dependence on folded travel-cost expressions and preserve useful routing guidance when capacity and demand names are unavailable.
